problems.title: Palindrome Number
problems.key_insight: Negative numbers and numbers ending in 0 (except 0) are not palindromes; reverse the last half digit by digit and compare it with the first half.
problems.statement: Return true if an integer reads the same backward as forward, without converting it to a string.
problems.google_follow_up: Why reverse only half of the digits instead of the whole number?

problems.title: Add Two Numbers
problems.key_pattern: Linked list walk with a carry
problems.key_insight: Walk both lists from the ones digit, add the digits plus the carry, write sum % 10, carry sum // 10, and continue while either list or the carry remains.
problems.statement: Two non-negative numbers are stored as linked lists in reverse digit order; return their sum as a linked list.
problems.google_follow_up: The digits are stored in forward order (Add Two Numbers II). What changes?

problems.title: Reverse Integer
problems.key_pattern: Digit-by-digit reverse with a range check
problems.key_insight: Pop digits with % 10 and // 10 from the absolute value, rebuild the reversed number, restore the sign, and return 0 if it leaves the 32-bit range.
problems.statement: Reverse the digits of a 32-bit signed integer; return 0 if the result does not fit in 32 bits.
problems.google_follow_up: In C++, how do you detect the overflow before it happens?

problems.title: Majority Element
problems.key_insight: Keep a candidate and a count: the same value adds 1, a different value subtracts 1, reset at 0; the value present more than n/2 times survives.
problems.statement: Return the element that appears more than n/2 times (it always exists).
edge_cases: The majority value is bunched at the end
problems.google_follow_up: Find every element that appears more than n/3 times (Majority Element II).

problems.title: Longest Common Prefix
problems.key_insight: Compare all strings character by character at the same position and stop at the first mismatch or at the end of the shortest string.
problems.statement: Return the longest common prefix shared by all strings in an array (an empty string if there is none).
edge_cases: An empty string in the list
problems.google_follow_up: You get many prefix questions about the same word list: would a trie help?

problems.title: Pow(x, n)
problems.key_insight: x^n = (x^(n // 2))^2, times x when n is odd; for negative n compute 1 / x^(-n). Only O(log n) multiplications.
problems.statement: Compute x raised to the power n, where n can be negative.
problems.google_follow_up: How does the same idea compute large powers modulo a number?

problems.title: Sqrt(x)
problems.key_insight: Find the largest m with m * m <= x by binary search between 0 and x.
problems.statement: Return the integer square root of a non-negative integer x (rounded down) without a built-in power or sqrt function.
problems.google_follow_up: How would you compute it to 5 decimal places?

problems.title: Rotate Array
problems.key_insight: Rotating right by k equals reversing the whole array, then reversing the first k items and the rest (use k % n).
problems.statement: Rotate an array to the right by k steps, in place.
edge_cases: k larger than the array length
problems.google_follow_up: Why do the three reversals give the right answer? Prove it on a small example.

problems.title: Merge Sorted Array
problems.key_insight: Fill nums1 from the end, placing the larger of the two largest remaining items, so nothing is overwritten before it is used.
problems.statement: Merge sorted nums2 into sorted nums1, which has room at the end, in place.
edge_cases: Every value in nums2 is smaller than nums1's
problems.google_follow_up: Why does filling from the front fail without extra space?

problems.title: Maximum Subarray
problems.key_insight: The best subarray ending at i is either nums[i] alone or nums[i] plus the best one ending at i - 1; keep the overall best.
problems.statement: Return the largest sum of a non-empty contiguous subarray.
problems.google_follow_up: Return the start and end positions too. What if the array is circular?

problems.title: Spiral Matrix
problems.key_insight: Keep top, bottom, left and right bounds; walk right, down, left and up, moving a bound inward after each side, and re-check the bounds before the last two sides.
problems.statement: Return all elements of an m x n matrix in spiral order.
problems.google_follow_up: Generate an n x n matrix filled in spiral order (Spiral Matrix II).

problems.title: Rotate Image
problems.key_insight: A 90-degree clockwise turn equals swapping matrix[i][j] with matrix[j][i] (transpose) and then reversing every row.
problems.statement: Rotate an n x n matrix 90 degrees clockwise, in place.
problems.google_follow_up: How do you rotate counter-clockwise instead?

problems.title: String to Integer (atoi)
problems.key_insight: Skip leading spaces, read one optional sign, read digits until a non-digit, then clamp the result to the 32-bit range.
problems.statement: Convert a string to a 32-bit signed integer like C's atoi: skip spaces, read a sign and digits, clamp on overflow.
problems.google_follow_up: Which five test cases would you write first, and why?

problems.title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
problems.key_insight: All numbers are positive, so grow the window on the right and shrink it from the left while the sum is still >= target, recording the shortest length.
problems.statement: Return the length of the shortest contiguous subarray whose sum is >= target (0 if none). All numbers are positive.
edge_cases: One element already reaches the target
problems.google_follow_up: What changes if the numbers can be negative?

problems.title: Find the Duplicate Number
problems.key_insight: Read each value as a pointer to the next index; the duplicate is where the cycle starts, found with slow and fast pointers without changing the array.
problems.statement: An array has n + 1 integers in the range 1..n; find the repeated number without modifying the array and with O(1) extra space.
problems.google_follow_up: Solve it with binary search on the value range instead.

problems.title: Jump Game
problems.key_insight: Track the farthest index reachable so far; if the current index is beyond it you are stuck, otherwise extend it with i + nums[i].
problems.statement: Each element is the maximum jump length from that index; return true if the last index can be reached from the first.
edge_cases: A zero you cannot jump over
problems.google_follow_up: Return the minimum number of jumps instead (Jump Game II).

problems.title: Next Permutation
problems.key_pattern: Find the pivot, swap, reverse the tail
problems.key_insight: From the right, find the first i with nums[i] < nums[i + 1]; swap it with the smallest larger value to its right, then reverse everything after i.
problems.statement: Rearrange the numbers into the next larger permutation in lexicographic order, in place (or the smallest order if none exists).
problems.google_follow_up: How would you jump straight to the k-th permutation?

problems.title: Find Peak Element
problems.key_insight: If nums[mid] < nums[mid + 1] a peak exists to the right, otherwise at mid or to the left; outside the array counts as minus infinity.
problems.statement: Return the index of any element that is greater than its neighbours, in O(log n) time.
problems.google_follow_up: Find a peak in a 2D grid (Find a Peak Element II).

problems.title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1)
problems.key_insight: Keep the values in a list and value -> index in a dict; to delete, move the last value into the deleted slot and pop the end.
problems.statement: Design a set with insert, remove and getRandom, each in O(1) average time.
edge_cases: Inserting a value that already exists
problems.google_follow_up: The same value may be added many times now (RandomizedCollection). What changes?

problems.title: Set Matrix Zeroes
problems.key_pattern: First row and column as markers
problems.key_insight: Use the first row and first column to remember which rows and columns to clear, with two flags for the first row and column themselves.
problems.statement: If an element is 0, set its whole row and column to 0, in place.
edge_cases: A zero in the first row or column
problems.google_follow_up: O(m + n) extra space is easy. How do you get to O(1)?

problems.title: Missing Number
problems.key_insight: The numbers 0..n add up to n(n + 1) / 2; subtract the actual sum (or XOR all indices and values) to get the missing one.
problems.statement: An array holds n distinct numbers from 0..n; return the one that is missing.
problems.google_follow_up: Why might XOR be safer than the sum in C++?

problems.title: Roman to Integer
problems.key_pattern: Left to right with a look-ahead
problems.key_insight: Add each symbol's value, but subtract it when a larger symbol comes next (IV, IX, XL ...).
problems.statement: Convert a Roman numeral string to an integer.
edge_cases: Subtractive pairs like IV and CM
problems.google_follow_up: Convert an integer back to a Roman numeral (Integer to Roman).

problems.title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
problems.key_insight: Binary-search a cut in the shorter array so the two left parts hold half of all elements and every left value <= every right value.
problems.statement: Return the median of two sorted arrays in O(log(m + n)) time.
problems.google_follow_up: Find the k-th smallest element of the two arrays instead.

problems.title: First Missing Positive
problems.key_pattern: The array as its own hash (cyclic placement)
problems.key_insight: Swap each value v in 1..n to index v - 1; afterwards the first index i with nums[i] != i + 1 gives the answer i + 1.
problems.statement: Return the smallest missing positive integer of an unsorted array in O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
problems.google_follow_up: Why do the swaps take only O(n) time in total?

problems.title: Minimum Window Substring
problems.key_insight: Grow the window on the right until it covers every needed character count, then shrink from the left while it still covers, keeping the smallest window.
problems.statement: Return the smallest substring of s that contains every character of t (with counts), or an empty string.
problems.google_follow_up: What if s arrives as a stream and t is very large?

drills.prompt: Return the largest sum of a non-empty contiguous subarray.
drills.pattern: Kadane's algorithm: The best subarray ending at i is either nums[i] alone or nums[i] plus the best one ending at i - 1; keep the overall best.

drills.prompt: Return the element that appears more than n/2 times (it always exists).
drills.pattern: Boyer-Moore voting: Keep a candidate and a count: the same value adds 1, a different value subtracts 1, reset at 0; the value present more than n/2 times survives.

drills.prompt: Rotate an array to the right by k steps, in place.
drills.pattern: Three reversals: Rotating right by k equals reversing the whole array, then reversing the first k items and the rest (use k % n).
drills.edge_case: k larger than the array length

drills.prompt: Return the length of the shortest contiguous subarray whose sum is >= target (0 if none). All numbers are positive.
drills.pattern: Shrinking sliding window: All numbers are positive, so grow the window on the right and shrink it from the left while the sum is still >= target, recording the shortest length.

drills.prompt: An array has n + 1 integers in the range 1..n; find the repeated number without modifying the array and with O(1) extra space.
drills.pattern: Cycle detection on index links (Floyd): Read each value as a pointer to the next index; the duplicate is where the cycle starts, found with slow and fast pointers without changing the array.

drills.prompt: Each element is the maximum jump length from that index; return true if the last index can be reached from the first.
drills.pattern: Greedy farthest reach: Track the farthest index reachable so far; if the current index is beyond it you are stuck, otherwise extend it with i + nums[i].

drills.prompt: Rearrange the numbers into the next larger permutation in lexicographic order, in place (or the smallest order if none exists).
drills.pattern: Find the pivot, swap, reverse the tail: From the right, find the first i with nums[i] < nums[i + 1]; swap it with the smallest larger value to its right, then reverse everything after i.

drills.prompt: Return the index of any element that is greater than its neighbours, in O(log n) time.
drills.pattern: Binary search on the slope: If nums[mid] < nums[mid + 1] a peak exists to the right, otherwise at mid or to the left; outside the array counts as minus infinity.

drills.prompt: Design a set with insert, remove and getRandom, each in O(1) average time.
drills.pattern: Array + hash map of positions: Keep the values in a list and value -> index in a dict; to delete, move the last value into the deleted slot and pop the end.
drills.complexity: O(1) average per operation time, O(n) space

drills.prompt: Return the smallest substring of s that contains every character of t (with counts), or an empty string.
drills.pattern: Sliding window with need counts: Grow the window on the right until it covers every needed character count, then shrink from the left while it still covers, keeping the smallest window.

drills.prompt:
Maximum subarray (Kadane):

  best = cur = 0
  for x in nums:
      cur = max(x, cur + x)
      best = max(best, cur)
  return best
drills.pattern: best starts at 0, so an all-negative array returns 0 instead of its largest number. Start with best = cur = nums[0] and loop from the second item.
